images.caption: The natural pool Collect Pond was located in lower Manhattan near present-day Foley Square. This watercolor of the site exemplifies the formulaic method of drawing taught at the Columbian Academy of Painting in New York City, founded by the brothers Archibald and Alexander Robertson. Both the hill at left and the willow tree at right were rendered in highly stylized fashion, with broad contours and schematic curving lines. Spatial depth was achieved with swaths of dark wash in the foreground, setting off the lighter forms in the distance. Indeed, the whole picture observes a kind of artistic etiquette embodied in the polite company of figures in the foreground.

images.filename: View of Manhattan from Centre Street shot tower.jpg
images.caption:
View north from the shot tower at 63 Centre Street. Center Street is on the right and Lafayette Street is on the left.
The crenellated rectangular building comprises freight depots for the New York and Harlem and New York and New Haven Railroads. It was replaced by the 1892 New York City Criminal Courts Building.
To its south, across Franklin Street, is the 1838 Halls of Justice, known as The Tombs. Its main entrance is on Centre Street; the long north-south building nearer Lafayette Street is the prison. On the site today is the Collect Pond Park.

See map: File:Perris Manhattan V. 1 Plate 014 publ. 1857.jpg.

images.caption: The entrance to the east end of Albert Capsouto Park (formerly CaVaLa), a triangle park bound by Canal Street, Laight Street, and Varick Street at 6th Avenue at the confluence of Tribeca, SoHo, and Hudson Square, Lower Manhattan. The park was opened in 2009. Pictured is an old map of lower Manhattan, showing the former Collect Pond which once occupied much of the area.
